{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZixzIQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDJjS8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 77, "title": "Resolve and implement live S-DSP BRR loop-directory reloads", "body": "## Problem

The DSP captures both BRR start and loop pointers at KON and retains the loop pointer for the voice’s lifetime. Changes to directory RAM, DIR or SRCN therefore cannot select a different loop destination without retriggering the voice.

This is the next bounded target identified by `latest_assessment`. Whether that lifetime snapshot matches hardware must be established from the documented directory-sampling rules before changing it. It affects ordinary BRR playback and requires no frontend changes.

## Expected outcome

Reconcile the S-DSP directory rules, then implement the demonstrated missing behavior for stable changes made during playback. Keep the existing sample-level architecture.

### Hardware contract to reconcile

Use these references, already cited by the repository:

- [Anomie/jwdonal S-DSP documentation, revision 1212](https://gist.github.com/nyanpasu64/a0d916ce6924912a7116682bf778e9a0#file-apudsp_jwdonal-txt): DIR, VxSRCN, BRR decoding and sound-generation ordering.
- [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm): DSP sample-directory registers and BRR end/loop behavior.
- Where prose leaves sampling ambiguous, consult [Shay Green/blargg’s original research implementation at the repository’s existing pinned revision](https://github.com/snes9xgit/snes9x/blob/8028d3b6ca994f21fdff220d513a08382e37afc3/apu/bapu/dsp/SPC_DSP.cpp), particularly the voice directory/address-fetch stages. Use it as attributed research evidence, not imported implementation or an output oracle.

These external references were not accessed during this repository-only planning pass. The repository’s [Issue #75 reconciliation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/3a6e051ad265ecd4dca9f456cf519e884c863926/docs/issue-75-validation.md#specification-reconciliation) establishes their provenance, but does not establish directory-reload semantics.

Verify and implement the following proposed stable-write contract, correcting any part contradicted by the references before deriving test expectations:

1. For voice `v`, directory entry address is `((DIR << 8) + 4 * SRCN[v]) mod 65536`. Its little-endian start word occupies entry offsets 0–1; its loop word occupies offsets 2–3.
2. With registers stable throughout KON initialization, playback starts from the selected start word. Later start-word changes do not restart an already playing voice.
3. A completed BRR block with end and loop bits set redirects playback to the loop destination selected by the documented live directory mechanism. Independently test changes to loop-word RAM, DIR and the playing voice’s SRCN, with writes completed well before the relevant fetch window.
4. Directory changes do not immediately redirect the current block or retrigger KON. Normal block progression, decoding/interpolation history, pitch phase and envelope state continue across the loop.
5. A changed loop destination remains changeable at subsequent loops. Preserve documented end-without-loop behavior and ENDX semantics.

Do not describe a physical loop-boundary RAM read merely because an implementation performs its lookup there. Establish whether hardware refreshes a pointer earlier or every sample, and explain why the selected stable-write cases have the same observable result. Exact subcycle edges, torn pointer writes and writes racing a fetch remain unresolved here. If the references do not establish a proposed rule, record that uncertainty instead of manufacturing a hardware requirement.

## Context and reproduction

Baseline: `3a6e051ad265ecd4dca9f456cf519e884c863926`; inspected HEAD matches it, with a clean working tree. Supplied context lists no open Issues and no completed live-directory improvement.

Concrete source evidence:

- [`Voice::loop_addr` and `Dsp::decode`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/3a6e051ad265ecd4dca9f456cf519e884c863926/crates/snes-core/src/dsp.rs#L4): the terminal loop branch uses the stored pointer.
- [`Dsp::sample` KON handling](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/3a6e051ad265ecd4dca9f456cf519e884c863926/crates/snes-core/src/dsp.rs#L143): DIR, SRCN and both directory words are read only when KON is processed.
- [Existing filter-0 loop test](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/3a6e051ad265ecd4dca9f456cf519e884c863926/crates/snes-core/src/dsp.rs#L665) seeds a private fixed loop pointer. [Existing ENDX regression](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/3a6e051ad265ecd4dca9f456cf519e884c863926/crates/snes-core/tests/regression.rs#L1152) exercises static directories across all eight voices.
- [`dsp_pitch.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/3a6e051ad265ecd4dca9f456cf519e884c863926/crates/snes-core/tests/dsp_pitch.rs) supplies original BRR data, bounded uploaded guests and numerical APU partition checks, but does not mutate the directory during playback.

Reproduce with original filter-0 BRR blocks having distinct constant sample values. Start voice A, finish its key-on delay, then change only its directory loop word to block B well before a terminal loop. Do not write KON again. The baseline continues selecting its captured destination. Repeat independently for DIR and SRCN; give new start and loop words different targets so an incorrect start-word lookup is detectable.

No tests were executed during planning. The source establishes snapshot behavior, not its hardware correctness.

### Scope and non-goals

Confine production changes to the directory lookup and BRR loop selection needed by the reconciled contract. Add focused tests and provenance/validation documentation. Avoid a DSP pipeline rewrite or new public inspection API.

Exclude subcycle DSP/SPC races, changes during KON delay, torn writes, echo/directory collisions, noise/pitch disputes, unrelated envelope ordering, reset retention and exhaustive BRR-filter work. Preserve current justified arithmetic and existing regressions; revise an earlier expectation only with explicit specification evidence.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record the resolved DIR/SRCN/start/loop rules with source sections, revisions and relevant excerpts or precise paraphrases. Separate documented facts, derived expectations and sample-API conventions. Correct unsupported prior contracts rather than retaining them because tests pass. Resolve the stable-write behavior before claiming an implementation fix.
- [ ] Implement every demonstrated mismatch within this scope. Add public-register numerical discriminators in `crates/snes-core/tests/dsp_directory.rs`; show that the relevant tests compile against the baseline and fail for the documented behavioral reason, then pass with the correction.
- [ ] Independently cover loop-word RAM edits, DIR changes and SRCN changes after KON; different start versus loop targets; no premature current-block redirect; a second live update on a later loop; and retriggering through the currently selected start entry. Use bounded checkpoints and independently derived stereo PCM, OUTX/ENVX and ENDX expectations rather than production-generated golden values.
- [ ] Cover directory-address carry/wrap, including `DIR=$ff, SRCN=$40` selecting entry `$0000`, and the last aligned entry’s loop word at `$fffe/$ffff`. Cover a BRR block whose payload crosses `$ffff` to `$0000`. Do not invent an unaligned directory word that cannot result from the address formula.
- [ ] Exercise simultaneous voices with different SRCN values: changing one SRCN or directory entry leaves the other voice’s selection intact; a shared DIR change selects each voice’s corresponding entry. Preserve ENDX reporting/clearing and end-without-loop controls. Include ordinary pitch and a multiple-nibble-per-sample case crossing a block boundary.
- [ ] Add an original SPC700 guest uploaded through the existing firmware-free protocol. The guest itself performs live directory/register changes without another KON, records discriminating OUTX/ENDX results and acknowledges bounded host checkpoints. Assert numerical host PCM as well. Document original MIT guest, directory and BRR-data provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`; acquire no commercial ROM, firmware or external sample assets.
- [ ] Compare whole versus irregular `Apu::tick` partitions at identical write/checkpoint boundaries through live changes and multiple loops. Compare every PCM sample and all 128 DSP registers, plus relevant guest RAM. Include independent numerical anchors; partition equality alone establishes determinism.
- [ ] Run and record these pre-merge gates using the README-supported toolchain:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test dsp_directory
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
(cd web && npx playwright install chromium && SNES_TEST_PORT=18085 npm test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds')
```

- [ ] Preserve existing envelope/hidden-envelope, noise, pitch, echo, ordered-mixing, controller, DMA/HDMA and PPU regressions. Keep the cleared games’ source pins, licenses, ROM hashes, replay routes, durations, freeze controls and numerical/live audio assertions. Mandatory cleared-game replays remain included by the browser command; unaudited optional game checks remain excluded.
- [ ] Record actual results, baseline failures, independent derivations and remaining uncertainty. No mandatory gate may remain failed, skipped or unperformed when claiming completion. Passing these bounded checks establishes neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.
- [ ] Retain all 24 inventory scopes: partial `cpu`, `bus`, `scheduler`, `dma`, `hdma`, `controllers`, `ppu-bg`, `ppu-offset`, `ppu-hires`, `ppu-mode7`, `ppu-objects`, `ppu-color`, `ppu-ports`, `ppu-display`, `spc`, `ipl`, `dsp-voices`, `dsp-noise`, `dsp-pitch`, `dsp-envelope`, `dsp-echo`, `dsp-timing`; unimplemented `ppu-raster`, `pal`. None becomes verified through this Issue. Remaining `dsp-voices` work includes independent filters 1–3 evidence, exhaustive interpolation phases, simultaneous key/mixing combinations and physical directory/key-event timing.

## Optional validation

Additional independently derived BRR patterns or already licensed source-built diagnostics. No commercial ROM acquisition or subjective listening is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
